redo_interpretation.why_not_gap1_completion: The rows prove exact grouped_reduction capability and device-column input-path improvements, but they do not prove that the Phoenix productized prepared execution/session runner executes across multiple Set-A probes.
redo_interpretation.why_keep_in_v3: The rows are reusable grouped_reduction engine evidence with exact row identities, CPU-reference agreement, source provenance records, and review/consensus closure.

serious_v2x_context.interpretation: The RayDB grouped_reduction rows do not override the failed broad V2.14 vs Phoenix V3 performance gate.

set_a_set_b_measurement_note.classification_for_future_all_app_scorec: treat bounded RayDB grouped_sum/count rows as Set-B or row-scoped controls unless they become part of a productized multi-phase execution path shared by other Set-A probes
set_a_set_b_measurement_note.reason: A single fused grouped_reduction row can be excellent engine evidence while still being too narrow to prove broad runtime superiority.

forbidden_readings: V3 is release-ready because RayDB grouped_reduction has large row-scoped wins.
RayDB is accelerated end to end.
The grouped_reduction rows prove broad V3-over-V2.x speedup.
The device-column rows prove true zero-copy.
The grouped_reduction rows complete Gap 1 productized execution path.

next_after_closure: Keep grouped_reduction in the current 13-row / 9-capability internal surface.
Do not spend more Phoenix time on RayDB-specific grouped_sum variants unless the work lands in a shared grouped_reduction or productized runner primitive.
Move the next Phoenix engineering focus to a second Set-A runner-backed family or a shared continuation path such as RTDBSCAN component_union.
Keep release and broad V3-over-V2 wording blocked until productized execution evidence and serious paired performance evidence justify a new review.

goal_level_decision_audit.decision: Close RayDB grouped_reduction for Phoenix redo as retained reusable engine evidence, not as V3 release evidence or Gap-1 completion.
goal_level_decision_audit.was_i_foolish: No. The decision preserves the strongest exact grouped_reduction rows while refusing to over-read them as broad V3 success.
goal_level_decision_audit.foolish_actions: It would be foolish to headline the large row-scoped speedups as V3 release performance, call RayDB a solved database product, or treat grouped_sum row closure as the productized execution path.
goal_level_decision_audit.other_path: Delete or demote all RayDB grouped_reduction work. That would throw away real reusable engine evidence and repeat the mistake of ignoring M0-M149 work.
goal_level_decision_audit.different_path_now: Retain the exact rows, document the non-release boundary, and move Phoenix work to shared runtime paths that can affect multiple probes.
